about: The `table_semantics` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain.

rows.grain: one row per MUNIS account
rows.what_it_answers: The chart of accounts — no money at all. One row per MUNIS account number split into fund, department, org and object, with its DESE function code, its name, whether it is revenue or expense, whether it is a roll-up or a detail account, and the years it appears.
rows.caution: department and function code.

rows.grain: one row per abbreviated account name
rows.what_it_answers: A decoder, not data: what each ten-character MUNIS abbreviation expands to, and the basis for each expansion.
rows.caution: The expansions are ours except where `basis` says otherwise.

rows.grain: one row per table per annual report
rows.what_it_answers: A catalogue of what EXISTS, not of what has been extracted. Every table found by reading all sixteen annual reports end to end: its printed heading verbatim, its pages, its grain, its printed total, and whether it is extractable.
rows.caution: A catalogue of what EXISTS, not of what has been extracted.

rows.grain: one row per extracted table
rows.what_it_answers: What was actually READ: which tables, from which pages, how many figures, and whether the extract is checkable against a printed total.
rows.caution: from which pages

rows.grain: one row per revenue line per year
rows.what_it_answers: Town REVENUE — every receipt line the annual reports print, by name and amount, per year, FY2011–FY2023. Only five years are `checked` against the report's own printed total.
rows.caution: as printed.

rows.grain: one row per page surveyed
rows.what_it_answers: A measurement of PAGES, not of figures: per page, the extraction mode, how many gutters and money tokens it holds, how many characters and rows. This is how the right instrument is chosen per page.
rows.caution: A survey, not data: it measures pages, it does not read figures.

rows.grain: one row per fee per year
rows.what_it_answers: The published fee a family pays to play: dollars per fiscal year × school level × item, with the date it was set and the document that set it. Includes family caps and sibling discounts.
rows.caution: by level and year.

rows.grain: one row per sport per season per metric
rows.what_it_answers: Per sport × season × level: participation COUNTS and DOLLAR figures mixed in one table, told apart by `metric`. `raw` keeps the value exactly as printed and `is_numeric` says whether it parsed, because some cells are text.

rows.grain: one row per printed total
rows.what_it_answers: Not data — checks. For each total the source prints, what our rows sum to, the difference, and whether it ties.

rows.grain: one row per athletics figure per year
rows.what_it_answers: Athletics money from BOTH sides, and these are three different quantities that must never be added: what the town appropriated from the general fund, what the revolving fund took IN, and what the revolving fund SPENT. Dollars per year with the basis and source document for each.
rows.caution: Appropriation, fund revenue and fund spending are three quantities. Never add two of them.

rows.grain: one row per ballot question
rows.what_it_answers: VOTES, not dollars — though each carries the amount at stake. Per ballot question: type, purpose, yes / no / blank counts, registered voters, turnout and the result.

rows.grain: one row per line per year per stage per variant
rows.what_it_answers: Dollar amounts per budget LINE from the district's budget documents — no counts, no people. Each figure carries the stage it represents (proposed / settled / actual) and, for FY27, which of four whole budget scenarios it belongs to. FY2014–FY2027, 9,503 figures, plus a flag where two documents state different amounts for the same line-year.
rows.caution: Split on `stage` AND `variant`. FY27 carries four whole budgets.
rows.default_query: SELECT f.fy, f.stage, f.variant, f.label, f.value, b.section, b.function_group, f.doc_id FROM budget_figure f LEFT JOIN budget_line b USING (line_key) ORDER BY f.fy, f.stage, f.value DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per budget line
rows.what_it_answers: The district's LINE LIST — no money at all. One row per budget line with its section, its function group and what kind of line it is. This is the dimension `budget_figure` and `workbook_figure` hang their dollars on.
rows.caution: with its section and function group.

rows.grain: one row per year
rows.what_it_answers: Per year, how capital spending was PAID FOR: free cash, taxation, unexpended prior-year capital, other. Dollars.

rows.grain: one row per project
rows.what_it_answers: The FY27 capital plan as proposed: project, department, cost, running cumulative, whether it was funded and from where.
rows.caution: ranked.

rows.grain: one row per budget line mapped to an account
rows.what_it_answers: EMPTY, deliberately. It would map a budget line to a ledger account, and it cannot: MUNIS truncates names to ten characters so `MS GUIDANC` and `HS GUIDANC` collide. Only the CATEGORY joins, through `account.function`.
rows.caution: Deliberately empty. MUNIS truncates to ten characters so MS GUIDANC and HS GUIDANC collide; only the CATEGORY can be joined, through account.function. Populating this would record an inference as a mapping.

rows.grain: one row per dataset per document
rows.what_it_answers: The join between an extracted dataset and the document it came from: which pages, how many rows, whether it reconciled, and the publisher's own label, size and checksum.

rows.grain: one row per district per year per measure
rows.what_it_answers: The state's published measures for EVERY Massachusetts district, per year: enrollment, per-pupil spending, selected populations. Each value carries whether it reconciles to DESE's own printed total.

rows.grain: one row per district per year per measure
rows.what_it_answers: DESE's ALL-FUNDS per-pupil expenditure figures for every district. All funds means grants and revolving funds are included, so these are NOT comparable with a general fund appropriation.
rows.caution: All-funds, so NOT comparable with the town's general fund appropriation.

rows.grain: one row per source document
rows.what_it_answers: One row per source document: its archive path, how it reached us, its publisher URL, whether that link still opens (`link_state`), whether our copy still matches the publisher's (`copy_state`), and both checksums. Also which columns a workbook HIDES from a reader.
rows.caution: `link_state` says whether the publisher's copy still opens; `copy_state` whether it still matches ours.

rows.grain: one row per planned extract
rows.what_it_answers: What is planned to be read out of the annual reports and what state each item is in — including items deliberately not attempted, and why.
rows.caution: and what state each is in.

rows.grain: one row per MUNIS period
rows.what_it_answers: What each MUNIS accounting period means and how many months of the year had elapsed. Period 13 is the year-end close after the lapse period, not a thirteenth month.
rows.caution: Period 13 is the year-end close after the lapse period, not a thirteenth month.

rows.grain: one row per line of the state's proof
rows.what_it_answers: The state's own line-by-line proof of certified free cash, for nine towns — every component with its role in the calculation. Dollars.
rows.caution: for nine towns.

rows.grain: one row per MUNIS fund
rows.what_it_answers: One row per MUNIS fund: its number, its name, what kind of fund it is and what restricts it. No money.
rows.caution: with its kind and restriction.

rows.grain: one row per transaction
rows.what_it_answers: TRANSACTIONS — the athletics revolving fund line by line: effective and posting dates, journal, references, vendor, amount, running balance, check and warrant numbers, and the comments the clerk typed. The only transaction-level data in the archive, obtained by records request.
rows.caution: from a records request.

rows.grain: one row per fund per year per period
rows.what_it_answers: Per fund per period: opening balance, revenue in, salaries, other expenditure, encumbered and closing balance. FY2026 period 9 only — and `opening_balance` is NULL for every one of the 61 funds.
rows.caution: spent and holds.
rows.default_query: SELECT a.fy, a.period, a.fund, f.name, f.kind, f.restriction, a.revenue, a.salaries, a.expenditure, a.encumbered, a.closing_balance FROM fund_activity a LEFT JOIN fund f USING (fund) ORDER BY a.closing_balance DESC LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per grant per year
rows.what_it_answers: Grant AWARDS: name, amount in dollars, who holds it, and the fiscal year — except one ESSER award that genuinely spans FY21–24, which is why `fy` is TEXT here.
rows.caution: by name and amount.

rows.grain: one row per grant per year
rows.what_it_answers: The same awards with their source addresses and checksums, plus whether documents disagree about an amount and whether it is ESSER money.
rows.caution: `fy` is TEXT — see grant_award.

rows.grain: one row per account per year per period per document
rows.what_it_answers: BOTH revenue and expense accounts from the town's MUNIS books, told apart by `account_type` — revenue is stored NEGATIVE. Six money measures per row: original appropriation, transfers, revised, expended, encumbered, available, plus percent used. Two grains in the same table (`level`): 67 department roll-ups and 916 detail accounts. FY2026 only, at two periods — 9 carries the department rows, 12 the account rows.
rows.caution: at a moment in the year.
rows.default_query: SELECT l.fy, l.period, l.account_id, a.name, a.fund_name, a.dept, a.function, a.account_type, a.level, l.original, l.revised, l.expended, l.encumbered, l.available FROM ledger_snapshot l JOIN account a USING (account_id) ORDER BY l.fy, l.period, l.account_id LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per line per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Every budget line × year × stage as EXTRACTED, before disagreements between documents are resolved. Dollars. This is the raw reading; `budget_figure` is the settled one.
rows.caution: every year

rows.grain: one row per source document
rows.what_it_answers: Not figures — a report on extraction. Per source document: how many data rows, how many carried a usable layout, how many fell short of the expected column count, and why a document was or was not usable.

rows.grain: one row per disagreeing reading
rows.what_it_answers: One row per disagreeing READING: where two documents state different dollar amounts for the same line-year, both values are kept with their source and the spread between them. Nothing here is resolved.
rows.caution: Kept rather than resolved. Which document is right is often not established.

rows.grain: one row per budget book line
rows.what_it_answers: The district's budget book in ITS OWN shape: one row per line with every year's column side by side (FY23 actual through the four FY27 scenarios) rather than unpivoted. Includes the workbook's own comments column, which is where the district explains a line to itself.
rows.caution: in its own shape and column order.

rows.grain: one row per assumption
rows.what_it_answers: Every assumption the money model rests on, what it rests on, and what single document would settle it.
rows.caution: with what would settle it.

rows.grain: one row per revenue account or fund or department
rows.what_it_answers: Our model, not measurement. One row per revenue account, fund or department: what we classified it as, HOW that was established, and WHY. 252 rows covering every money node in the school and town diagrams.
rows.caution: `how` and `why` carry the basis so a classification can be argued with.

rows.grain: one row per traced edge
rows.what_it_answers: Where a restricted fund's money is PERMITTED to go, with the statute or grant award that permits it. An edge is a presumption about purpose, never an observation of spending.
rows.caution: An edge is the statute or grant award — a PRESUMPTION about purpose, never an observation of spending.

rows.grain: one row per gap
rows.what_it_answers: The honest list of what CANNOT be answered — per side (money in, money out), what is missing and why the published documents do not close it.
rows.caution: This table is the honest list of what cannot be answered.

rows.grain: one row per account per report
rows.what_it_answers: The MUNIS chart of accounts exactly as DELIVERED, before our normalisation — including the report parameters (`totals_only`, `suppress_zero`) that decide what a report shows and therefore what is missing from it.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Out-of-district special education tuition in DOLLARS, split private vs collaborative, per year per stage. Not a count of children — `placement_counts` is that, and the two do not divide into each other.
rows.caution: private and collaborative.

rows.grain: one row per year
rows.what_it_answers: CHILDREN, not dollars. Students placed outside the district, split collaborative / day / residential, measured on 1 March each year from SIMS Report 7. FY2013–FY2025. Carries its own checks: whether the parts sum to the total, and whether each year agrees with the next year's restatement of it.
rows.caution: split collaborative/day/residential.

rows.grain: one row per rate
rows.what_it_answers: Every rate and fee the model uses: the value, what kind of value it is, when it was set, when it expires, its source document and cell reference, and whether the model actually uses it.
rows.caution: with where it was set.

rows.grain: one row per anomaly
rows.what_it_answers: Things found while reading the annual reports that need a person: a total that does not tie, a heading that moved, a column that vanished.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: APPROPRIATIONS as the annual reports print them — the largest extract here, 4,665 rows across sixteen years. Values sit in ORDINAL columns (v1..v8) whose meaning changes page to page; `column_meaning` names them where the table states an identity that fixes them, and says `not established` where it does not.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Read `column_meaning` and split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Capital project funds as the annual reports print them: appropriated, expended, encumbered and balance, per article.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Outstanding DEBT and repayment schedules as the annual reports print them. Dollars, town-wide — school building debt is inside these figures and is not separated out.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Departmental activity tables — permits issued, inspections done, cases handled. Mostly COUNTS rather than dollars, and what is counted differs by department and by year.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Election results as the annual reports print them: candidates, offices and vote counts in ordinal columns.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Enrollment counts and MCAS results as the annual reports print them. Mixed measures in ordinal columns; read `column_meaning` before using any of them.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: GROSS WAGES paid per named employee per year, as the annual reports print them. 3,545 rows. Actual pay rather than budget, including overtime and details.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Figures for Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical School as the annual reports print them. A DIFFERENT DISTRICT: Lunenburg pays it an assessment, and its figures must never be added to Lunenburg's own schools.
rows.caution: Monty Tech is a DIFFERENT DISTRICT. Never add it to Lunenburg's schools.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Names and offices of town officials as each annual report lists them. No money.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Trust fund balances and activity as the annual reports print them.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Assessed property VALUATION by class, as the annual reports print it. Dollars — and the base the tax levy is computed on.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Counts of births, marriages and deaths as the annual reports print them.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS. Split on `status`.

rows.grain: one row per revenue source per year
rows.what_it_answers: The checked subset of the above joined to our classification: the printed name, our normalised key, what KIND of revenue it is (levy, state aid, local receipt, transfer, one-time), the amount, and the document and page it came from. Five years.
rows.caution: with our classification of what KIND it is.

rows.grain: one row per printed roster title
rows.what_it_answers: Our classification of each printed roster title into a role category and grade, with how it was classified. Judgement, recorded so it can be disputed.

rows.grain: one row per school fund
rows.what_it_answers: The schools' own funds at one moment (FY26 period 9): per fund, revenue received, salaries paid, other expenditure, encumbered, and the balance left. Dollars.

rows.grain: one row per fund per year
rows.what_it_answers: Every fund OUTSIDE the general appropriation, FY2011–FY2025: balance brought forward, receipts, disbursements, balance carried forward. Grants, revolving funds and gifts that pay for real staff and appear nowhere in the appropriation. Dollars.
rows.caution: fifteen years

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Budgeted DOLLARS for special education paraprofessionals, split by school, per year per stage. A budget line, never a headcount.
rows.caution: A budget line, not a headcount.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Budgeted DOLLARS for special education teachers, split by school, per year per stage. A budget line, never a headcount.
rows.caution: A budget line, not a headcount.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: Budgeted DOLLARS for special education transportation, per year per stage.

rows.grain: one row per printed roster title
rows.what_it_answers: A lookup, not data: each printed roster title, how many times it was seen, and the position it maps to.

rows.grain: one row per school per position per year
rows.what_it_answers: Counts of the names above, per school × position × year. A count of names the town printed. It is not a staffing level and cannot be turned into one.
rows.caution: A count of NAMES, with no FTE and no funding source. It is not a staffing level.

rows.grain: one row per person per year
rows.what_it_answers: PEOPLE — one row per name the town printed, per year, with the school, the page, the printed job title and our classification of it. FY2011–FY2025, 3,815 entries. No FTE, no salary, no funding source, and undated within the year.
rows.caution: name by name

rows.grain: one row per figure the town stated
rows.what_it_answers: Figures the town or district ASSERTED in their own words, with the quote, who said it, when, and what it supersedes. Claims, kept as claims.
rows.caution: with the quote.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: One dollar total per year per stage — the district's own stated total expenses, as each document states it.

rows.grain: one row per year per stage
rows.what_it_answers: One dollar total per year per stage — the district's own stated total salaries.

rows.grain: one row per department
rows.what_it_answers: The town's 67 departments at FY26 period 9: appropriation, transfers, revised, expended, encumbered, available and percent used. EXPENSE side only, department grain only.
rows.caution: by department.

rows.grain: one row per function group
rows.what_it_answers: Computed, not read: per function group, how far spending ran from budget across years — budgeted, spent, net, gross, churn, and the best and worst years.
rows.caution: across years.

rows.grain: one row per worksheet row per year per column
rows.what_it_answers: The FY27 budget workbook unpivoted to one row per worksheet row × year × column, so every figure is quotable by its spreadsheet coordinate. `column_kind` says which printed column — final_budget, actual_to_date, encumbered_to_date. Dollars only.
rows.caution: every cell quotable by its row.
rows.default_query: SELECT w.fy, w.column_kind, w.row_kind, w.row, b.label, w.value FROM workbook_figure w LEFT JOIN budget_line b USING (line_key) ORDER BY w.fy, w.row LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per table in this database
rows.what_it_answers: This page's own source. One row per table: its role, whose money it is, how finely it resolves money, its grain, what it holds, and what goes wrong if it is used carelessly.
rows.caution: Self-describing, and checked both ways: a table with no row here fails the build, and a row naming a table that no longer exists fails it too.

rows.grain: one row per DISTINCT column name across the whole database
rows.what_it_answers: One row per DISTINCT column name across the whole database: what it means, its unit, whether it is published or ours, and the caution attached to it.
rows.caution: Keyed on the NAME, not on table plus name, because `v1` and `status` mean the same dangerous thing everywhere they appear. Where a name genuinely differs by table, the table entry says so.

rows.grain: one row per fund per year
rows.what_it_answers: The special revenue schedule READ from the rendered page rather than OCR'd: balance brought forward, total receipts, total disbursements, balance carried forward, per fund. **The only version of this table that ties to its own printed grand total** — FY2022, 167 funds, all four columns to the penny and every row balancing.
rows.caution: A figure read off an image is a READING, not a published number — same status as the OCR's. It is trustworthy because the report's own printed total and the table's own identity both check it, not because a model produced it. Years that do not tie are not in here.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, page, [group], fund, forward, receipts, disbursements, carried, row_ties FROM special_revenue_read ORDER BY fy, page, rowid LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per edition
rows.what_it_answers: The GRAND TOTAL each annual report PRINTS for the special revenue schedule, quoted with its page. Four columns.
rows.caution: This is the independent check on `special_revenue_read`, so it must be read off the page and never computed from our own rows — the OCR misread this very figure by $1,010 and the reconciliation was measured against it for months.

rows.grain: one row per line per fund column per year
rows.what_it_answers: What the town HOLDS, read from the COMBINED BALANCE SHEET — assets, liabilities and fund equity across six fund columns (general, special revenue, enterprise, capital project, trust and agency, long-term debt). Everything else in this archive measures money MOVING; this is the only table that measures what is sitting there.
rows.caution: Read from the page, like `special_revenue_read`. It is trusted because three checks hold: each column foots to its own printed total, the sheet's identity (liabilities + fund equity = assets) holds per column, and special revenue + enterprise fund equity ties to the special revenue schedule's carried-forward total — an INDEPENDENT document. One printed sheet does not balance itself (FY2019 trust and agency, $657,297.35 apart); that is the town's print, recorded not corrected.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, section, line, fund, amount FROM balance_sheet ORDER BY fy, section, line LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per printed total per fund column per year
rows.what_it_answers: The totals each balance sheet PRINTS — total assets, total liabilities, total fund equity — quoted with the page they appear on.
rows.caution: The independent check on `balance_sheet`, so it must be read off the page and never computed from our own rows.

rows.grain: one row per line per fund column per printing per year
rows.what_it_answers: What the four ENTERPRISE funds hold at 30 June — Sewer, Water, Solid Waste and PEG Access, side by side, with a memorandum-only total column. Read from the COMBINING BALANCE SHEET — ENTERPRISE FUNDS, which is the only balance sheet FY2024 and FY2025 print; neither report contains the town-wide combined balance sheet `balance_sheet` holds for FY2011–FY2023.
rows.caution: RATEPAYER MONEY. Sewer and water user charges, betterments, trash fees and cable franchise money — none of it is available to the town's general operations and none of it is a tax dollar. This is NOT an extension of `balance_sheet`: that table's `enterprise` value is one of six fund-type COLUMNS on a different sheet, and the two must never be unioned. FY2024 prints the same sheet TWICE (printed pages 21 and 28), so `printing` is 1 or 2 and must be collapsed on before anything is summed — summing across it doubles the money. FY2024's memorandum column is $102,000.00 out on two offsetting lines; that is the town's print, recorded not corrected. Only cells that print a figure are recorded; the sheet's 0.00 and '-' template cells are not rows here.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, section, line, fund, amount FROM enterprise_balance_sheet WHERE printing = 1 ORDER BY fy, section, line LIMIT 1000

rows.grain: one row per printed total per fund column per printing per year
rows.what_it_answers: The totals the enterprise balance sheet PRINTS — Total Assets, Total Liabilities, Total Fund Equity, Total Liabilities and Fund Equity, and the sheet's own PROOF row — quoted with the raw cell text and the page.
rows.caution: The independent check on `enterprise_balance_sheet`, so it must be read off the page and never computed from our own rows. The PROOF row is the sheet's own self-check and is what a reading is reconciled to. FY2025 prints its Proof as '(0.00)' and '-' in different columns; the amount recorded is 0.00 and the raw glyph is in `quote`.
